outcome: Still open in general: since 26 January 2024 it has gained a full proof for four variables in equal degrees 5 and 7 (Wang–Zhang, arXiv 25 Aug 2026, whose main results the authors attribute to a generative-AI workflow), equal-degree results through degree d+2 (Boij–Dannetun–Lundqvist, 5 May 2026), and partial non-equal-degree results (Blomenhofer–Casarotti, 12 Sep 2025); I found no resolution of the unrestricted conjecture.
problem_asks: (1) The Wikipedia statement, as fetched: for k generic homogeneous polynomials g_1,…,g_k in n variables over ℂ with degrees a_1,…,a_k, the Hilbert series of ℂ[x_1,…,x_n]/(g_1,…,g_k) equals the truncation, at its first non-positive coefficient, of (1+t+t²+…)^n · ∏(1−t^{a_i}). So the claim is coefficient by coefficient about the Hilbert function. (2) Scope: it asserts this for every number of variables n, every number k of forms, and every degree sequence a_1,…,a_k, not for some of them. (3) Strength: the generic-forms claim is an equality (the strong reading). The literature I read also states a weak form, which asserts only an inequality in the expected direction; the Wikipedia lead as fetched does not distinguish strong from weak, so both are listed. (4) Setting: Wikipedia says ℂ; BDL and Trung work over infinite fields of any characteristic; Wang–Zhang works over characteristic-zero fields. The bullet's own name is 'Fröberg conjecture on the Hilbert functions of a set of forms'.

events.what_happened: Qihang Wang and Dongming Zhang, 'Fröberg's Conjecture for Quintics and Septics in Four Variables', arXiv:2608.24797 (math.AC). v1 posted 25 Aug 2026, v2 26 Aug, v3 27 Aug. Claims, over any characteristic-zero field, Fröberg's predicted Hilbert series for ideals generated by r general forms of equal degree d in four variables, for every r ≥ 1, when d = 5 and d = 7. The proof reduces each r to finitely many endpoint rank computations on Macaulay multiplication matrices, each certified by an explicit minor. I found no journal version, referee report or public commentary on it.
events.revisions: v1 25 Aug 2026: the v1 abstract contains no AI sentence, and the v1 comments read 'ancillary exact verification programs and certificate'. v2 26 Aug 2026. v3 27 Aug 2026, comment: 'revises the acknowledgements and automated-assistance disclosure. The theorem statements and proofs are unchanged.' The current abstract carries the generative-AI sentence; whether v2 did is not established.
events.delivers: Restricted to n = 4 variables, equal degree d ∈ {5, 7}, characteristic zero (the open set U_{d,r} depends on d and r), and all r ≥ 1: the predicted truncated series for R/(f_1,…,f_r) with f_i general forms of degree d. The classical cases r ≤ 5 and the equal-degree theorem through degree d+2 of Boij–Dannetun–Lundqvist are cited as known; the new input is for 6 ≤ r ≤ 11 when d = 5 and 6 ≤ r ≤ 21 when d = 7. Covers one number of variables, two degrees, equal degrees only.
events.remains: Everything else in problem_asks: every n other than 4; every d other than 5 and 7 in four variables; unequal degree sequences; the weak form and any positive-characteristic statement. The authors say 'the unrestricted Fröberg conjecture remains outside the scope of the paper'.
events.directly_checkable: The proof is a computation, not a construction. Quintics: ten endpoint matrices built from 21 sparse forms. Septics: fifteen endpoint matrices from a family of 120 integral forms. Each new certificate records a maximal square minor that is nonzero mod 2, hence a nonzero integer, which gives full rank over the characteristic-zero field and, by Zariski openness, over every characteristic-zero field. The ancillary files, per the search excerpt of the paper, are two Python 3 standard-library verifiers (froberg_quintics_verifier.py; froberg_septics_verifier.py, which reads a JSON certificate) and an exact septic certificate; the quintic check also recomputes ranks mod 101 and mod 1009; the authors report PASS. I did not download or run them.
events.doubts: No independent check or public review found. The argument is computational, so its correctness depends on the certified endpoint ranks; the logic as I read the summary (mod-2-nonzero minor ⇒ nonzero integer ⇒ full rank over ℚ, then Zariski openness) looks sound, but I did not check the certificates. By the authors' own account the main results came from a generative-AI workflow across three named systems, with 'repeated self-critique and alternative derivations'; this is disclosed, not hidden, but the disclosure changed across versions (v3 revised it) and the v1 abstract had no AI sentence, so the v1 and v2 disclosure text in the PDF needs reading. The acknowledgements thank Ralf Fröberg and Samuel Lundqvist for correspondence and comments on 'scope and context', which is not a verification. The acknowledgement also credits 'Gewu Intelligence Lab' for the research environment; I found nothing about that lab.
events.direction: Consistent with Fröberg's prediction: it claims the predicted truncated series is the actual Hilbert series in the stated cases. No counterexample is claimed.

events.what_happened: Mats Boij, Eric Dannetun and Samuel Lundqvist, 'Independence of generic forms and the Fröberg conjecture', arXiv:2605.03872 (math.AC), v1 posted 5 May 2026, the only version listed. Shows the Fröberg conjecture holds in the second non-trivial degree d+2 for ideals generated by generic forms of degree d > 2 over an infinite field; shows it holds up to degree 2d−1 when the number of variables is sufficiently large; Theorem 6 extends the range to d+d' for d' ≤ 2100 under a dimension inequality, using a MATLAB sign-change check.
events.revisions: v1 5 May 2026 only, as of my fetch.
events.delivers: For equal-degree generic forms of degree d > 2, equality with the predicted truncated series in every degree up to d+2, for any number r of forms (Theorem 1 as read; no bound on n stated). For n sufficiently large, the series is correct up to degree 2d−1 (Theorem 2, any d > 1). Theorem 6: correct up to degree d+d' for 2 ≤ d' ≤ 2100 when the dimension inequality dim R_{d+d'} ≥ (dim R_{d'})² holds and a numerical check holds. Restricted to equal degrees.
events.remains: Unequal degree sequences; degrees beyond d+d' for d' > 2100 and degrees where the inequality fails; d' ≥ d (the authors say 'there are Koszul relations' and 'a completely different approach is needed'); the inequality g_{d,d'}(x) ≤ g_{d,d'}(n−1), which the authors believe but have not proved; and the full conjecture for all n.
events.directly_checkable: Numerical verifications, not constructions: Macaulay2 computations over finite fields with small primes for the cases d = 4 with n ≤ 5 and d = 3 with small n (the fetched text gives both n ≤ 15 and n ≤ 21 for d = 3; Lemma 8 covers larger n); a MATLAB check that g_{d,d'} has at most one sign change; the bibliography links a GitHub repository titled 'Computer calculations - Independence of generic forms and the Fröberg conjecture', which I did not open.
events.doubts: No active doubt found. The authors' own limits are the numerical bound d' ≤ 2100, an unproven inequality, and the stated failure of the method at d' ≥ d. The two different ranges for the d = 3 computations in the fetched text (n ≤ 15 and n ≤ 21) could not be reconciled from the HTML. No written verification found; the paper is cited and used as input by Wang–Zhang and by Shapiro's v2, neither of which reports checking it.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture: confirms the predicted Hilbert function in the stated degree ranges for equal-degree generic forms. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: Mats Boij and Samuel Lundqvist, 'On the Hilbert series of ideals generated by general linear forms', arXiv:2608.22823 (math.AC, cross-listed math.AG), v1 posted 24 Aug 2026, the only version listed. Determines the Hilbert series of ideals generated by d'-th powers of n+2 general linear forms in n variables and uses it to show that the Iarrobino–Fröberg conjecture fails for all sufficiently large n; the abstract also reports counterexamples to a Weak Lefschetz conjecture and some n+3 cases. I read only the abstract page.
events.delivers: About powers of general linear forms (the Iarrobino–Fröberg variant), not general forms: that variant fails for large n. It says nothing about the generic-forms conjecture as stated.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: the conjecture for general forms of arbitrary degree.
events.doubts: Not peer reviewed as far as I found. Only the abstract was read, not the body.
events.direction: Cuts against the Iarrobino–Fröberg variant (powers of linear forms), per the abstract. It bears on the stated problem only by analogy.
events.object: Not described in what I read: the abstract describes a family of ideals generated by d'-th powers of n+2 general linear forms in n variables, whose Hilbert series is determined, and says the variant fails for large n, without naming a specific instance.

events.what_happened: Boris Shapiro, 'Generic μ-power ideals, fat points, and symbolic powers', arXiv:2609.27965 (math.AC). Version 1 is dated 23 Aug 2026 in arXiv's submission history, which conflicts with the 2609 identifier prefix (September); unresolved. v1 answers negatively Problem F of Fröberg, Lundqvist, Oneto and Shapiro (FLOS18): whether r generic μ-power forms (μ a non-pure partition of d) have the Hilbert series G_{n,d,r} predicted for r general forms of degree d. Per the v1 HTML rendering, Corollary 6.4 is a degree-14 ternary example: five forms L_i^13·M_i (L_i pairwise non-proportional), whose ideal has HF(24) ≥ 1 where the predicted coefficient is 0. Positive for r ≤ n+1 via Stanley's theorem. Version 2 (26 Sep 2026) is rewritten: different abstract, and the v2 text I read has no Section 6 and no Corollary 6.4.
events.revisions: v1 23 Aug 2026 per arXiv submission history (the 2609 identifier suggests September 2026; unresolved). v2 26 Sep 2026: rewritten, new abstract, the Section 6 counterexample is absent from the v2 text I read, and the AI statement changes to 'ChatGPT/Codex and Claude'.
events.delivers: Shows that for non-pure μ, generic μ-power ideals need not have the Hilbert series predicted for general forms (negative answer to Problem F, via a master obstruction criterion, and the degree-14 example in v1); positive for r ≤ n+1. The generators are μ-powers, not general forms, so this is not a counterexample to the generic-forms statement.
events.remains: The Fröberg conjecture for general forms (all of problem_asks) is untouched. The v1 result is about a different family of generators.
events.directly_checkable: The v1 example is a concrete degree-14 ternary computation: five forms F_i = L_i^13·M_i and the claimed value HF(24) ≥ 1 against a coefficient of 0. The v1 AI statement, as read, says the numerical assertions are reproducible from an accompanying script; I did not run it.
events.doubts: The two versions disagree materially: v1 has Section 6 and Corollary 6.4 (credited to GPT-5.6); the v2 text I read has no Section 6, a different abstract and a general AI statement. The arXiv identifier and the v1 date are inconsistent. Not peer reviewed as far as I found. v2 also cites Blomenhofer–Casarotti and Boij–Dannetun–Lundqvist, but I found no citation of Wang–Zhang in v2.
events.direction: Cuts against Problem F (μ-power generators versus the Fröberg-predicted series): a negative answer for non-pure μ. Does not contradict the Fröberg conjecture for general forms, since the generators are not general.
events.object: v1 Corollary 6.4: five forms F_i = L_i^13·M_i in ℂ[x,y,z] of degree 14, with L_i pairwise non-proportional, for which the ideal has Hilbert function ≥ 1 at degree 24 while the predicted coefficient is 0. Explicit (the forms are given), not existence-only, per the v1 text as rendered. Applies only to the μ-power variant.

events.what_happened: Alexander Taveira Blomenhofer and Alex Casarotti, 'On defectivity of joins, reducible secants and Fröberg's conjecture', arXiv:2509.10443 (math.AG). v1 posted 12 Sep 2025, the only version listed. Introduces r-defectivity for vector bundles on quasi-projective varieties. Uses it to prove 'several previously unknown cases of Fröberg's conjecture', including Theorem 4.1 for forms of non-equal degree over ℂ under a numerical condition (17) on the degrees, and a fat-point postulation result.
events.revisions: v1 only listed on the arXiv abstract page. I found no journal reference.
events.delivers: Over ℂ, for forms f_1,…,f_r of degrees d_1 ≤ … ≤ d_k with multiplicities α_i: when condition (17) holds for every i, the graded piece of the ideal in degree d_k+ℓ has the expected dimension, which gives the predicted Hilbert function in that degree. A range of degree types under a numerical hypothesis, not a general statement.
events.remains: The conjecture for all degree sequences and all ℓ. The authors call Fröberg's conjecture 'a long-standing open problem' and say their results 'leave a small gap of cases, where we cannot prove nondefectivity'.
events.doubts: The HTML rendering of Theorem 4.1's second clause ends 'the fat point scheme is empty', which fits Theorem 4.2 rather than a Hilbert-function statement. I read this as a probable copy error, not verified in the PDF. The authors state their own gap. I found no journal version.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture: partial confirmations for some non-equal-degree types under a numerical hypothesis. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: Ralf Fröberg and Clas Löfwall, 'Generic forms', arXiv:2504.13591 (math.AC). v1 posted 18 Apr 2025; v2 7 Oct 2025; v3 19 Jul 2026 ('New title. First three sections reworked'; a search excerpt gives the later title 'Generic forms and algebras'). Covers genericity of presentations and minimal Hilbert series. Per the abstract: generic presentations are characterised by a countable intersection of Zariski open sets over ℝ or ℂ; the minimal series is stated as a commutative conjecture; there is a non-commutative quadratic conjecture; for a generic quadratic presentation, products x_i·f_j are linearly independent or generate A_3; the Koszul dual of a generic presentation is generic in some cases.

events.direction: No direction on the Hilbert series of general forms.

summary: The problem is open in general. Since 26 January 2024 the literature has moved in four ways. (a) Wang and Zhang (arXiv:2608.24797, posted 25 August 2026) prove the predicted Hilbert series for ideals generated by r general quintics and by r general septics in four variables, for every r, over any characteristic-zero field, using a computation with explicit certificates; the authors state in the abstract that 'the main results of this paper were obtained through a generative-AI workflow using OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol, Anthropic Claude Fable 5, and Grok 4.6', and the v3 disclosure revised the acknowledgements and automated-assistance text. The v1 abstract has no AI sentence, so the disclosure in the v1 and v2 PDFs was not read. I found no verification. (b) Boij, Dannetun and Lundqvist (arXiv:2605.03872, 5 May 2026) prove equality in every degree up to d+2 for equal-degree generic forms of degree d > 2, with an extension to 2d−1 for large n and a further numerical range; they use Macaulay2 and MATLAB computations and state some limits. (c) Blomenhofer and Casarotti (arXiv:2509.10443, 12 September 2025) prove some non-equal-degree cases under a numerical hypothesis, and state a gap. (d) Park's 2009 claim of the conjecture in characteristic zero (arXiv:0910.3830 v1) was dropped from v2 after a 'crutial misunderstanding' comment; that is a withdrawal in effect and predates the window. The Shapiro preprint (arXiv:2609.27965) and the Boij–Lundqvist preprint (arXiv:2608.22823) concern variants, not general forms: Shapiro's answers negatively a question about μ-power generators (v1 gives a degree-14 counterexample credited to GPT-5.6, with Claude credited for other sections; v2 is a rewritten paper with a different abstract, and the v2 text I read has no such counterexample), and Boij–Lundqvist show the Iarrobino–Fröberg variant fails for large n. The Fröberg–Löfwall v3 and the Fröberg Betti-number paper do not bear on the Hilbert function. Earlier partial results (Fröberg 1985 for n = 2, Anick 1986 for n = 3, Stanley 1980 and Watanabe 1987 for r = n+1, Hochster–Laksov 1987 for degree d+1, Nicklasson 2015 and Nenashev 2015 for many equal-degree cases, Trung 2018 for r ≤ n+2 via Pardue's equivalence) are recorded as events, although several were read only through secondary sources. The Wikipedia lead, last edited 18 June 2025, gives the statement and cites only the 1985 and 1997 papers. The Emergent Mind open-problems entry lists the conjecture as a question with no status, and cites the 2025–2026 preprints. Close calls. (i) Whether the Wang–Zhang result counts as a settled 'case' or as a restricted case is for the judging pass; it is clearly restricted to one n and two degrees. (ii) Whether the AI attribution is load-bearing: the abstract says the main results came from the workflow, which is the authors' own account, but the disclosure does not say which system did which step. (iii) Shapiro's v1 counterexample is to a different question (Problem F); I did not treat it as bearing on the stated problem except as context. (iv) The arXiv identifier 2609.27965 is inconsistent with the 23 August v1 date, reported by the arXiv abstract page; I did not resolve this. No Lean or Coq formalisation was found. The AI search covered GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Fable 5, Grok 4.6 and Gewu Intelligence Lab; no other AI-credited work on this conjecture was found.
competing_reading: A strict reading counts only events that settle a whole case of the stated problem (all n and all degree sequences), and so finds no resolution: each event fixes n, the degrees, or a degree range. A looser reading treats the conjecture as a family of coefficient-wise claims, so that the Boij–Dannetun–Lundqvist equality in degree d+2 for all r, and the Wang–Zhang full series for n = 4 with d ∈ {5, 7}, each fix a set of coefficients and count as growth of a settled set. On the AI question: the authors' abstract attributes the Wang–Zhang main results to a workflow, which is load-bearing on its face; a stricter reader may say that a joint sentence naming three systems does not show which system supplied which mathematics, so the attribution is to the workflow, not to any one model.
what_would_settle_it: (1) An independent run of the Wang–Zhang ancillary verifiers and an independent recomputation of the endpoint ranks in another computer-algebra system. (2) The PDF disclosure text in v1, v2 and v3 of arXiv:2608.24797, to see what changed and whether the AI statement was added or altered. (3) Any journal or expert verification of the Wang–Zhang result. (4) The full text of Boij–Dannetun–Lundqvist, to fix the statements of Theorems 1, 2 and 6, the computation scope (the d = 3 range), and the GitHub computations. (5) The arXiv record for 2609.27965: the true v1 date, and whether the degree-14 counterexample was removed from the paper or from the record. (6) The original texts of Nenashev (arXiv:1512.04324), Hochster–Laksov (1987), Anick (1986), Stanley (1980) and Watanabe (1987), to fix their dates and ranges. (7) Whether any later paper cites Wang–Zhang; I checked only Shapiro's v2, which does not.

event.what_happened: Alexander Taveira Blomenhofer and Alex Casarotti, 'On defectivity of joins, reducible secants and Fröberg's conjecture', arXiv:2509.10443 (math.AG). v1 posted 12 Sep 2025, the only version listed. Introduces r-defectivity for vector bundles on quasi-projective varieties. Uses it to prove 'several previously unknown cases of Fröberg's conjecture', including Theorem 4.1 for forms of non-equal degree over ℂ under a numerical condition (17) on the degrees, and a fat-point postulation result.
event.revisions: v1 only listed on the arXiv abstract page. I found no journal reference.
event.delivers: Over ℂ, for forms f_1,…,f_r of degrees d_1 ≤ … ≤ d_k with multiplicities α_i: when condition (17) holds for every i, the graded piece of the ideal in degree d_k+ℓ has the expected dimension, which gives the predicted Hilbert function in that degree. A range of degree types under a numerical hypothesis, not a general statement.
event.remains: The conjecture for all degree sequences and all ℓ. The authors call Fröberg's conjecture 'a long-standing open problem' and say their results 'leave a small gap of cases, where we cannot prove nondefectivity'.
event.doubts: The HTML rendering of Theorem 4.1's second clause ends 'the fat point scheme is empty', which fits Theorem 4.2 rather than a Hilbert-function statement. I read this as a probable copy error, not verified in the PDF. The authors state their own gap. I found no journal version.
event.direction: Consistent with the conjecture: partial confirmations for some non-equal-degree types under a numerical hypothesis. No counterexample.

judgement.why: The statement covers all n, all numbers of forms and all degree sequences, so every restricted result counts as a case. Wang–Zhang (n=4, d=5,7) is a credible case. It is unreviewed because the rank certificates need a program to check them, not a check by hand. Its abstract says the main results were obtained through the generative-AI workflow, which is the authors' own account of AI producing the mathematics, so the role is generated, credited to all three systems because the disclosure does not divide the work among them. Boij–Dannetun–Lundqvist and Blomenhofer–Casarotti are unreviewed human cases. Shapiro and Boij–Lundqvist concern μ-powers and powers of linear forms. Those are variants and say nothing about general forms, so Shapiro's v1 counterexample is not a counterexample to this statement. Shapiro's AI role is assisted, from its own quote, but the event is a variant and the harness discards it. Park's v1 claim was withdrawn by the author. Older journal results are digested cases before the snapshot.
judgement.doubts: The Wang–Zhang AI disclosure changed between versions and the v1/v2 PDF text was not read. Nobody has independently run its verifiers. One could argue for 'checkable' because explicit certificates and verifiers exist, but checking them is a computation, not a simple decisive check. Several pre-2024 ranges come only from secondary sources.
